articles.title: Carly Rae Jepsen works round-the-clock in Day and Night
articles.description: Music history is full of excellent releases made in the wake of new motherhood - from Lauryn Hill's Miseducation to Eartheater's Heavenly Body this year. Carly Rae Jepsen has a habit of releasing albums in two, typically releasing a B-side album for each cycle. These storied traditions came together on Sept. 18 for Day and Night , the pop star's eighth studio release and first double album arriving right after the birth of her first child. While not quite her Ray of Light , this outing features a tremendous expansion of Jepsen's sonic palette and some more feathers in the cap of contemporary pop's most consistent should've-been-a-hit-maker. With 24 songs for 24 hours, the album is split into 'day' and 'night' sides. The Day side songs share an autumnal wistfulness with a focus on live instrumentals Jepsen hasn't spotlighted so strongly since her debut . The Night side gives her classic synthpop a clubbier spin. There's no doubt Jepsen had little difficulty filling up 84 minutes - fans will recall her claims of writing 200 songs for Dedicated . The diverse production choices help the time go by quickly, but I question the inclusion of some of these tracks (' That's Just Me " goes in one ear and out the other). The album's singles are well selected for the most part. " On Wires " and " After All " mark the public's introduction to the album's day side, and both remain among the strongest tracks on the record. The emphatic guitar-driven chorus of "On Wires" (with the classic Jepsen brass in the back of the mix) marks a radical departure from her typical sound. Meanwhile, "After All," a soulful and hazy fall-time picture of family life, opens the album as a natural evolution of the disco sounds from her previous The Loveliest Time . The Night side was represented in the singles department by " Don't Leave Me on the Dancefloor ," which evokes ABBA in its bright piano keys and Robyn's patent ' sad banger ' style. " Motivation " marks well-explored territory as a catchy, almost embarrassingly sincere dance-pop ode to found family. The single " Versailles ," released alongside the album, is perhaps most telling for Jepsen's intentions with her latest project. Stuttering piano appears and disappears as she switches in and out of a slower, ballad-esque tempo and a dance track to dissolve in. These adventurous production choices crop up in several other tracks, from the mild psychedelic distortions in " Something Tragic " to the closer of the Day side, " Just a Little Walk on the Moon ." Her vocals in the bossa nova influenced song sound like they're emerging from an evening radio, as the album prepares for the night side of life. " Gimme your time, gimme your nights, gimme your days " she demands on " Habits of Creatures " - and who can deny her? Jepsen's B-sides do tend to have the better songs - I staunchly maintain both Dedicated: Side B and The Loveliest Time are superior to their A-side counterparts - and this double album does not mark an exception. While the stripped back and instrument-based soundscape of the Day side do not always synergise with the pop star's strengths, her forays into new dancefloor territory on the Night side yield more consistently magical results. " Never Let a Good Thing Die " immediately launches listeners from the Day side into the club, pulsating with jittery beats before expertly transitioning into an expansive outro. Right after, " Amalfi Coast " recalls Jessie Ware's nu-disco while blending a vocoder and synth to glorious house effect. Jepsen does not stray far from her usual lyrical grounds across the album, but in " Patience Power Passion " she delights in the irresistible bounce of the chorus , while in " Diver " she pulls out enough metaphors to please a high school English teacher. Her warehouse of dance references expands with the build-up to the garage-style beat of " Near or Far ," merging with her poppy sensibilities where " No Labels, I Love You " conjures up classic house for everyone to get up and dance. Fittingly, she draws the curtains on " Super Sage ," an ethereal and enveloping track filled with love. Day and Night is among Jepsen's more mellow and less immediate records, along the tone of The Loneliest Time . It is also perhaps her most ambitious album so far - released during one of the busiest periods of her life (keep an ear out for her upcoming 10 Things I Hate About You musical ). "My joke is that I'm at some point going to write a memoir, and it'll be called The Year We Did Everything at Once, " she described in an interview with Elle . For an album which reflects this breadth, all of it - the new, the familiar, the great, the less-good - feels at home in the sonic world she has constructed in her musicianship. This stylistic expansion is a new springboard to continue growing her flawless discography (yes, including Tug of War ). As the world of dance-pop evolves, Carly Rae Jepsen strengthens her niche and keeps her loyal listeners excited to run away with her once more.

articles.title: Spiraling Up: 6 Projects Using Spiral Ramps for Vertical Movement
articles.description: In most architectural projects, vertical circulation is expressed as a purely functional element , tucked away behind fire-rated doors or an elevator core. However, sometimes architects also use spirals when trying to resolve site elevation changes. Given the right scale, these elements allow for a more artistic formal expression that serves both utilitarian and aesthetic purposes without relying on mechanical lifts or stairwells. Structural systems like cantilevered steel trusses and reinforced concrete decks allow these spiral elements to extend outward as sheltered entry canopies or wind around open central atriums. Functionally, these circulation paths may be expressed in several ways: as stairs like the Itamaraty Palace in Brasilia, or as ramps, which can offer the possibility to reduce mobility barriers for visitors. In both cases, the spiral can provide smooth transitions across varied floor levels while maintaining an unobstructed line-of-sight throughout the program.

articles.title: Windows 11’s optional September update tries to fix Bluetooth again
articles.description: Microsoft has released September’s optional Windows update, known as KB5124010 for Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2 . It significantly improves the Bluetooth functionality of Windows 11 and optimizes File Explorer, plus adds a few minor features here and there. What’s new in KB5124010? Bluetooth remains a perennial issue with Windows 11, which Microsoft has been trying to address for months . If you’ve been suffering through unreliable or broken Bluetooth connections, update KB5124010 may offer some relief—it should improve Bluetooth device connectivity, even more than the Windows 11 Bluetooth fixes from June . File Explorer now offers an improved preview for files downloaded from the web, eliminating the need to manually unblock the preview for each individual file. File Explorer also automatically displays a preview of all downloaded files again (with the exception of HTML files, for which there is a “Preview” button). Emoji fans will like that KB5124010 rolls out the Emoji 17.0 set for Windows 11, allowing you to use a number of new emojis, such as the distorted face, the ballet dancer, the fight cloud, and the hairy creature. Microsoft claims to have fixed a bug that made it difficult to personalize Windows (for example, wallpapers). Device-Independent Bitmap (DIB) files are now also supported for desktop backgrounds, and Microsoft has added support for background images in slideshow mode across various desktop configurations. Further improvements include some quality-of-life boosts, like being able to set app windows to always open maximized, the ability to remap the Copilot key, and a new Tips widget that offers Windows guidance. All of these features and improvements are being gradually rolled out to all users, so it’s possible that you won’t see them immediately after installing the update. If you don’t, wait a few days and try again. In addition to new features and improvements, the optional KB5124010 update also fixes a serious issue with File History . Whereas the feature had stopped working correctly after September Patch Tuesday, it’s now fixed immediately after installing KB5124010. Note that this update also removes the PC-to-PC Migration tool, which previously made it possible to migrate files and settings directly from one PC to a new PC being set up. That process should now handled by Windows Backup and Restore instead. How to install the KB5124010 update Windows 11 doesn’t automatically install KB5124010 because it’s an optional preview update. You’ll need to search for KB5124010 manually via Windows Settings → Windows Update → Advanced options → Optional updates. Alternatively, you can download this optional update directly from the Microsoft Update Catalog . Next month, on October 13th, Microsoft will roll out all the benefits of KB5124010 to all users with the mandatory October Patch Tuesday update. If you can wait that long, don’t want to try out any of the new features straight away, and aren’t bothered by the faulty File History feature, then you don’t need to install this optional update.

articles.title: Buying a motherboard? Check this amazing site first
articles.description: Shopping for a motherboard can get surprisingly complicated. A board might advertise five M.2 slots and a stack of PCIe slots, which sounds great... until you find out that using one of them can slow down or disable another. Enter MoboMaps . This free site lays out a motherboard’s PCIe connections in a simple interactive map, showing how lanes run from the CPU and chipset to the GPU, M.2 slots, and other expansion slots. The visual layout is a much easier way to spot potential conflicts than digging through a 100-page motherboard manual looking for one tiny footnote. One of my coworkers here at PCWorld introduced me to this site and I plan to use it before I install any new boards on a build. MoboMaps is especially useful if you’re planning to install a lot of hardware. On some boards, for example, putting an NVMe SSD in a certain M.2 slot can knock your graphics card connection from x16 down to x8. MoboMaps has a handy performance checker that lets you toggle different components and see which ones might end up sharing bandwidth. It’s also useful before you buy anything. You can filter boards by brand, chipset, form factor, PCIe generation, number of M.2 slots, USB4 support, and whether they share lanes with the GPU. There’s even a side-by-side comparison tool. MoboMaps currently covers more than 200 motherboards including the most popular brands. If you’re putting together a gaming PC or adding another SSD, MoboMaps is a great tool to check before making a purchase or starting a new build.
